lines.text: To comfort you. I wot well where he is.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Hark ye, your Romeo will be here at night.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I’ll to him, he is hid at Lawrence’ cell.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O find him, give this ring to my true knight,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And bid him come to take his last farewell.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Friar Lawrence.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Romeo, come forth; come forth, thou fearful man.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Affliction is enanmour’d of thy parts

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And thou art wedded to calamity.
Enter Romeo.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Father, what news? What is the Prince’s doom?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: What sorrow craves acquaintance at my hand,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: That I yet know not?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Too familiar

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Is my dear son with such sour company.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: I bring thee tidings of the Prince’s doom.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: What less than doomsday is the Prince’s doom?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: A gentler judgment vanish’d from his lips,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Not body’s death, but body’s banishment.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Ha, banishment? Be merciful, say death;

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: For exile hath more terror in his look,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Much more than death. Do not say banishment.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hence from Verona art thou banished.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Be patient, for the world is broad and wide.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: There is no world without Verona walls,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: But purgatory, torture, hell itself.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Hence banished is banish’d from the world,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And world’s exile is death. Then banished

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Is death misterm’d. Calling death banished,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Thou cutt’st my head off with a golden axe,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And smilest upon the stroke that murders me.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: O deadly sin, O rude unthankfulness!

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thy fault our law calls death, but the kind Prince,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Taking thy part, hath brush’d aside the law,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And turn’d that black word death to banishment.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: This is dear mercy, and thou see’st it not.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: ’Tis torture, and not mercy. Heaven is here

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Where Juliet lives, and every cat and dog,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And little mouse, every unworthy thing,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Live here in heaven and may look on her,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: But Romeo may not. More validity,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: More honourable state, more courtship lives

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: In carrion flies than Romeo. They may seize

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: On the white wonder of dear Juliet’s hand,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And steal immortal blessing from her lips,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Who, even in pure and vestal modesty

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Still blush, as thinking their own kisses sin.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: But Romeo may not, he is banished.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: This may flies do, when I from this must fly.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: They are free men but I am banished.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And say’st thou yet that exile is not death?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Hadst thou no poison mix’d, no sharp-ground knife,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: No sudden mean of death, though ne’er so mean,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: But banished to kill me? Banished?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: O Friar, the damned use that word in hell.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Howling attends it. How hast thou the heart,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Being a divine, a ghostly confessor,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: A sin-absolver, and my friend profess’d,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: To mangle me with that word banished?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou fond mad man, hear me speak a little,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: O, thou wilt speak again of banishment.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: I’ll give thee armour to keep off that word,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Adversity’s sweet milk, philosophy,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To comfort thee, though thou art banished.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Yet banished? Hang up philosophy.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Unless philosophy can make a Juliet,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Displant a town, reverse a Prince’s doom,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: It helps not, it prevails not, talk no more.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: O, then I see that mad men have no ears.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: How should they, when that wise men have no eyes?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Let me dispute with thee of thy estate.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Thou canst not speak of that thou dost not feel.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Wert thou as young as I, Juliet thy love,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: An hour but married, Tybalt murdered,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Doting like me, and like me banished,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Then mightst thou speak, then mightst thou tear thy hair,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And fall upon the ground as I do now,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Taking the measure of an unmade grave.
[_Knocking within._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Arise; one knocks. Good Romeo, hide thyself.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Not I, unless the breath of heartsick groans

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Mist-like infold me from the search of eyes.
[_Knocking._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hark, how they knock!—Who’s there?—Romeo, arise,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou wilt be taken.—Stay awhile.—Stand up.
[_Knocking._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Run to my study.—By-and-by.—God’s will,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: What simpleness is this.—I come, I come.
[_Knocking._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Who knocks so hard? Whence come you, what’s your will?
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Let me come in, and you shall know my errand.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I come from Lady Juliet.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Welcome then.
Enter Nurse.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O holy Friar, O, tell me, holy Friar,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Where is my lady’s lord, where’s Romeo?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: There on the ground, with his own tears made drunk.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O, he is even in my mistress’ case.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Just in her case! O woeful sympathy!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Piteous predicament. Even so lies she,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Blubbering and weeping, weeping and blubbering.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Stand up, stand up; stand, and you be a man.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: For Juliet’s sake, for her sake, rise and stand.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Why should you fall into so deep an O?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Nurse.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Ah sir, ah sir, death’s the end of all.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Spakest thou of Juliet? How is it with her?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Doth not she think me an old murderer,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Now I have stain’d the childhood of our joy

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: With blood remov’d but little from her own?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Where is she? And how doth she? And what says

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: My conceal’d lady to our cancell’d love?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O, she says nothing, sir, but weeps and weeps;

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: And now falls on her bed, and then starts up,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: And Tybalt calls, and then on Romeo cries,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: And then down falls again.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: As if that name,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Shot from the deadly level of a gun,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Did murder her, as that name’s cursed hand

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Murder’d her kinsman. O, tell me, Friar, tell me,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: In what vile part of this anatomy

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Doth my name lodge? Tell me, that I may sack

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: The hateful mansion.
[_Drawing his sword._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hold thy desperate hand.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Art thou a man? Thy form cries out thou art.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thy tears are womanish, thy wild acts denote

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: The unreasonable fury of a beast.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Unseemly woman in a seeming man,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And ill-beseeming beast in seeming both!

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou hast amaz’d me. By my holy order,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: I thought thy disposition better temper’d.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hast thou slain Tybalt? Wilt thou slay thyself?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And slay thy lady, that in thy life lives,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: By doing damned hate upon thyself?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Why rail’st thou on thy birth, the heaven and earth?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Since birth, and heaven and earth, all three do meet

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: In thee at once; which thou at once wouldst lose.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Fie, fie, thou sham’st thy shape, thy love, thy wit,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Which, like a usurer, abound’st in all,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And usest none in that true use indeed

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Which should bedeck thy shape, thy love, thy wit.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thy noble shape is but a form of wax,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Digressing from the valour of a man;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thy dear love sworn but hollow perjury,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Killing that love which thou hast vow’d to cherish;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thy wit, that ornament to shape and love,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Misshapen in the conduct of them both,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Like powder in a skilless soldier’s flask,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Is set afire by thine own ignorance,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And thou dismember’d with thine own defence.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: What, rouse thee, man. Thy Juliet is alive,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: For whose dear sake thou wast but lately dead.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: There art thou happy. Tybalt would kill thee,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: But thou slew’st Tybalt; there art thou happy.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: The law that threaten’d death becomes thy friend,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And turns it to exile; there art thou happy.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: A pack of blessings light upon thy back;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Happiness courts thee in her best array;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: But like a misshaped and sullen wench,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou putt’st up thy Fortune and thy love.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Take heed, take heed, for such die miserable.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Go, get thee to thy love as was decreed,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Ascend her chamber, hence and comfort her.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: But look thou stay not till the watch be set,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: For then thou canst not pass to Mantua;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Where thou shalt live till we can find a time

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To blaze your marriage, reconcile your friends,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Beg pardon of the Prince, and call thee back

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: With twenty hundred thousand times more joy

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Than thou went’st forth in lamentation.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Go before, Nurse. Commend me to thy lady,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And bid her hasten all the house to bed,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Which heavy sorrow makes them apt unto.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Romeo is coming.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O Lord, I could have stay’d here all the night

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: To hear good counsel. O, what learning is!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: My lord, I’ll tell my lady you will come.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Do so, and bid my sweet prepare to chide.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Here sir, a ring she bid me give you, sir.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Hie you, make haste, for it grows very late.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: How well my comfort is reviv’d by this.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Go hence, good night, and here stands all your state:

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Either be gone before the watch be set,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Or by the break of day disguis’d from hence.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Sojourn in Mantua. I’ll find out your man,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And he shall signify from time to time

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Every good hap to you that chances here.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Give me thy hand; ’tis late; farewell; good night.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: But that a joy past joy calls out on me,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: It were a grief so brief to part with thee.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Farewell.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Capulet, Lady Capulet and Paris.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Things have fallen out, sir, so unluckily

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: That we have had no time to move our daughter.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Look you, she lov’d her kinsman Tybalt dearly,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And so did I. Well, we were born to die.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: ’Tis very late; she’ll not come down tonight.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I promise you, but for your company,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I would have been abed an hour ago.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: These times of woe afford no tune to woo.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Madam, good night. Commend me to your daughter.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: I will, and know her mind early tomorrow;

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Tonight she’s mew’d up to her heaviness.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Sir Paris, I will make a desperate tender

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Of my child’s love. I think she will be rul’d

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: In all respects by me; nay more, I doubt it not.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Wife, go you to her ere you go to bed,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Acquaint her here of my son Paris’ love,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And bid her, mark you me, on Wednesday next,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: But, soft, what day is this?

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Monday, my lord.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Monday! Ha, ha! Well, Wednesday is too soon,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: A Thursday let it be; a Thursday, tell her,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: She shall be married to this noble earl.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Will you be ready? Do you like this haste?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: We’ll keep no great ado,—a friend or two,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: For, hark you, Tybalt being slain so late,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: It may be thought we held him carelessly,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Being our kinsman, if we revel much.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Therefore we’ll have some half a dozen friends,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And there an end. But what say you to Thursday?

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: My lord, I would that Thursday were tomorrow.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Well, get you gone. A Thursday be it then.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Go you to Juliet ere you go to bed,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Prepare her, wife, against this wedding day.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Farewell, my lord.—Light to my chamber, ho!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Afore me, it is so very very late that we

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: May call it early by and by. Good night.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: An open Gallery to Juliet’s Chamber, overlooking the Garden.

lines.text: Enter Romeo and Juliet.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Wilt thou be gone? It is not yet near day.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: It was the nightingale, and not the lark,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That pierc’d the fearful hollow of thine ear;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Nightly she sings on yond pomegranate tree.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Believe me, love, it was the nightingale.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: It was the lark, the herald of the morn,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: No nightingale. Look, love, what envious streaks

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Do lace the severing clouds in yonder east.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Night’s candles are burnt out, and jocund day

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Stands tiptoe on the misty mountain tops.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I must be gone and live, or stay and die.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Yond light is not daylight, I know it, I.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: It is some meteor that the sun exhales

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To be to thee this night a torchbearer

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And light thee on thy way to Mantua.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Therefore stay yet, thou need’st not to be gone.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Let me be ta’en, let me be put to death,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I am content, so thou wilt have it so.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I’ll say yon grey is not the morning’s eye,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: ’Tis but the pale reflex of Cynthia’s brow.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Nor that is not the lark whose notes do beat

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: The vaulty heaven so high above our heads.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I have more care to stay than will to go.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Come, death, and welcome. Juliet wills it so.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: How is’t, my soul? Let’s talk. It is not day.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: It is, it is! Hie hence, be gone, away.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: It is the lark that sings so out of tune,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Straining harsh discords and unpleasing sharps.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Some say the lark makes sweet division;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: This doth not so, for she divideth us.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Some say the lark and loathed toad change eyes.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O, now I would they had chang’d voices too,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Since arm from arm that voice doth us affray,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Hunting thee hence with hunt’s-up to the day.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O now be gone, more light and light it grows.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: More light and light, more dark and dark our woes.
Enter Nurse.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Madam.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Nurse?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Your lady mother is coming to your chamber.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: The day is broke, be wary, look about.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Then, window, let day in, and let life out.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Farewell, farewell, one kiss, and I’ll descend.
[_Descends._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Art thou gone so? Love, lord, ay husband, friend,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I must hear from thee every day in the hour,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: For in a minute there are many days.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O, by this count I shall be much in years

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Ere I again behold my Romeo.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Farewell!

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I will omit no opportunity

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: That may convey my greetings, love, to thee.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O thinkest thou we shall ever meet again?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I doubt it not, and all these woes shall serve

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: For sweet discourses in our time to come.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O God! I have an ill-divining soul!

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Methinks I see thee, now thou art so low,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: As one dead in the bottom of a tomb.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Either my eyesight fails, or thou look’st pale.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And trust me, love, in my eye so do you.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Dry sorrow drinks our blood. Adieu, adieu.
[_Exit below._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O Fortune, Fortune! All men call thee fickle,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: If thou art fickle, what dost thou with him

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That is renown’d for faith? Be fickle, Fortune;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: For then, I hope thou wilt not keep him long

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: But send him back.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Ho, daughter, are you up?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Who is’t that calls? Is it my lady mother?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Is she not down so late, or up so early?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What unaccustom’d cause procures her hither?
Enter Lady Capulet.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Why, how now, Juliet?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Madam, I am not well.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Evermore weeping for your cousin’s death?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: What, wilt thou wash him from his grave with tears?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: And if thou couldst, thou couldst not make him live.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Therefore have done: some grief shows much of love,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: But much of grief shows still some want of wit.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Yet let me weep for such a feeling loss.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: So shall you feel the loss, but not the friend

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Which you weep for.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Feeling so the loss,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I cannot choose but ever weep the friend.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Well, girl, thou weep’st not so much for his death

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: As that the villain lives which slaughter’d him.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What villain, madam?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: That same villain Romeo.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Villain and he be many miles asunder.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: God pardon him. I do, with all my heart.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And yet no man like he doth grieve my heart.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: That is because the traitor murderer lives.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Ay madam, from the reach of these my hands.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Would none but I might venge my cousin’s death.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: We will have vengeance for it, fear thou not.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Then weep no more. I’ll send to one in Mantua,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Where that same banish’d runagate doth live,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Shall give him such an unaccustom’d dram

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: That he shall soon keep Tybalt company:

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: And then I hope thou wilt be satisfied.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Indeed I never shall be satisfied

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: With Romeo till I behold him—dead—

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Is my poor heart so for a kinsman vex’d.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Madam, if you could find out but a man

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To bear a poison, I would temper it,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That Romeo should upon receipt thereof,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Soon sleep in quiet. O, how my heart abhors

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To hear him nam’d, and cannot come to him,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To wreak the love I bore my cousin

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Upon his body that hath slaughter’d him.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Find thou the means, and I’ll find such a man.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: But now I’ll tell thee joyful tidings, girl.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And joy comes well in such a needy time.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What are they, I beseech your ladyship?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Well, well, thou hast a careful father, child;

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: One who to put thee from thy heaviness,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Hath sorted out a sudden day of joy,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: That thou expects not, nor I look’d not for.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Madam, in happy time, what day is that?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Marry, my child, early next Thursday morn

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: The gallant, young, and noble gentleman,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: The County Paris, at Saint Peter’s Church,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Shall happily make thee there a joyful bride.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Now by Saint Peter’s Church, and Peter too,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: He shall not make me there a joyful bride.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I wonder at this haste, that I must wed

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Ere he that should be husband comes to woo.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I pray you tell my lord and father, madam,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I will not marry yet; and when I do, I swear

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: It shall be Romeo, whom you know I hate,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Rather than Paris. These are news indeed.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Here comes your father, tell him so yourself,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: And see how he will take it at your hands.
Enter Capulet and Nurse.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: When the sun sets, the air doth drizzle dew;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: But for the sunset of my brother’s son

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: It rains downright.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: How now? A conduit, girl? What, still in tears?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Evermore showering? In one little body

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Thou counterfeits a bark, a sea, a wind.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: For still thy eyes, which I may call the sea,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Do ebb and flow with tears; the bark thy body is,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Sailing in this salt flood, the winds, thy sighs,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Who raging with thy tears and they with them,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Without a sudden calm will overset

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Thy tempest-tossed body. How now, wife?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Have you deliver’d to her our decree?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Ay, sir; but she will none, she gives you thanks.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: I would the fool were married to her grave.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Soft. Take me with you, take me with you, wife.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: How, will she none? Doth she not give us thanks?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Is she not proud? Doth she not count her blest,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Unworthy as she is, that we have wrought

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: So worthy a gentleman to be her bridegroom?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Not proud you have, but thankful that you have.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Proud can I never be of what I hate;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: But thankful even for hate that is meant love.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: How now, how now, chopp’d logic? What is this?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Proud, and, I thank you, and I thank you not;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And yet not proud. Mistress minion you,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Thank me no thankings, nor proud me no prouds,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: But fettle your fine joints ’gainst Thursday next

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: To go with Paris to Saint Peter’s Church,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Or I will drag thee on a hurdle thither.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Out, you green-sickness carrion! Out, you baggage!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: You tallow-face!

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Fie, fie! What, are you mad?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Good father, I beseech you on my knees,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Hear me with patience but to speak a word.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Hang thee young baggage, disobedient wretch!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I tell thee what,—get thee to church a Thursday,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Or never after look me in the face.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Speak not, reply not, do not answer me.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: My fingers itch. Wife, we scarce thought us blest

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: That God had lent us but this only child;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: But now I see this one is one too much,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And that we have a curse in having her.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Out on her, hilding.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: God in heaven bless her.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: You are to blame, my lord, to rate her so.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And why, my lady wisdom? Hold your tongue,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Good prudence; smatter with your gossips, go.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I speak no treason.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: O God ye good-en!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: May not one speak?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Peace, you mumbling fool!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Utter your gravity o’er a gossip’s bowl,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: For here we need it not.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: You are too hot.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: God’s bread, it makes me mad!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Day, night, hour, ride, time, work, play,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Alone, in company, still my care hath been

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: To have her match’d, and having now provided

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: A gentleman of noble parentage,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Of fair demesnes, youthful, and nobly allied,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Stuff’d, as they say, with honourable parts,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Proportion’d as one’s thought would wish a man,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And then to have a wretched puling fool,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: A whining mammet, in her fortune’s tender,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: To answer, ‘I’ll not wed, I cannot love,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I am too young, I pray you pardon me.’

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: But, and you will not wed, I’ll pardon you.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Graze where you will, you shall not house with me.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Look to’t, think on’t, I do not use to jest.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Thursday is near; lay hand on heart, advise.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And you be mine, I’ll give you to my friend;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And you be not, hang, beg, starve, die in the streets,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: For by my soul, I’ll ne’er acknowledge thee,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Nor what is mine shall never do thee good.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Trust to’t, bethink you, I’ll not be forsworn.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Is there no pity sitting in the clouds,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That sees into the bottom of my grief?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O sweet my mother, cast me not away,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Delay this marriage for a month, a week,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or, if you do not, make the bridal bed

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: In that dim monument where Tybalt lies.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Talk not to me, for I’ll not speak a word.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Do as thou wilt, for I have done with thee.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O God! O Nurse, how shall this be prevented?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: My husband is on earth, my faith in heaven.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: How shall that faith return again to earth,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Unless that husband send it me from heaven

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: By leaving earth? Comfort me, counsel me.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Alack, alack, that heaven should practise stratagems

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Upon so soft a subject as myself.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What say’st thou? Hast thou not a word of joy?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Some comfort, Nurse.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Faith, here it is.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Romeo is banished; and all the world to nothing

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: That he dares ne’er come back to challenge you.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Or if he do, it needs must be by stealth.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Then, since the case so stands as now it doth,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I think it best you married with the County.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O, he’s a lovely gentleman.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Romeo’s a dishclout to him. An eagle, madam,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Hath not so green, so quick, so fair an eye

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: As Paris hath. Beshrew my very heart,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I think you are happy in this second match,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: For it excels your first: or if it did not,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Your first is dead, or ’twere as good he were,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: As living here and you no use of him.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Speakest thou from thy heart?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: And from my soul too,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Or else beshrew them both.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Amen.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Well, thou hast comforted me marvellous much.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Go in, and tell my lady I am gone,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Having displeas’d my father, to Lawrence’ cell,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To make confession and to be absolv’d.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Marry, I will; and this is wisely done.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Ancient damnation! O most wicked fiend!

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Is it more sin to wish me thus forsworn,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or to dispraise my lord with that same tongue

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Which she hath prais’d him with above compare

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: So many thousand times? Go, counsellor.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Thou and my bosom henceforth shall be twain.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I’ll to the Friar to know his remedy.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: If all else fail, myself have power to die.
[_Exit._]
Enter Friar Lawrence and Paris.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: On Thursday, sir? The time is very short.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: My father Capulet will have it so;

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: And I am nothing slow to slack his haste.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: You say you do not know the lady’s mind.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Uneven is the course; I like it not.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Immoderately she weeps for Tybalt’s death,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: And therefore have I little talk’d of love;

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: For Venus smiles not in a house of tears.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Now, sir, her father counts it dangerous

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: That she do give her sorrow so much sway;

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: And in his wisdom, hastes our marriage,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: To stop the inundation of her tears,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Which, too much minded by herself alone,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: May be put from her by society.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Now do you know the reason of this haste.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: I would I knew not why it should be slow’d.—

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Look, sir, here comes the lady toward my cell.
Enter Juliet.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Happily met, my lady and my wife!

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That may be, sir, when I may be a wife.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: That may be, must be, love, on Thursday next.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What must be shall be.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: That’s a certain text.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Come you to make confession to this father?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To answer that, I should confess to you.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Do not deny to him that you love me.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I will confess to you that I love him.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: So will ye, I am sure, that you love me.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: If I do so, it will be of more price,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Being spoke behind your back than to your face.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Poor soul, thy face is much abus’d with tears.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: The tears have got small victory by that;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: For it was bad enough before their spite.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Thou wrong’st it more than tears with that report.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That is no slander, sir, which is a truth,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And what I spake, I spake it to my face.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Thy face is mine, and thou hast slander’d it.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: It may be so, for it is not mine own.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Are you at leisure, holy father, now,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or shall I come to you at evening mass?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: My leisure serves me, pensive daughter, now.—

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: My lord, we must entreat the time alone.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: God shield I should disturb devotion!—

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Juliet, on Thursday early will I rouse ye,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Till then, adieu; and keep this holy kiss.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O shut the door, and when thou hast done so,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Come weep with me, past hope, past cure, past help!

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: O Juliet, I already know thy grief;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: It strains me past the compass of my wits.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: I hear thou must, and nothing may prorogue it,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: On Thursday next be married to this County.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Tell me not, Friar, that thou hear’st of this,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Unless thou tell me how I may prevent it.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: If in thy wisdom, thou canst give no help,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Do thou but call my resolution wise,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And with this knife I’ll help it presently.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: God join’d my heart and Romeo’s, thou our hands;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And ere this hand, by thee to Romeo’s seal’d,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Shall be the label to another deed,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or my true heart with treacherous revolt

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Turn to another, this shall slay them both.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Therefore, out of thy long-experienc’d time,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Give me some present counsel, or behold

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: ’Twixt my extremes and me this bloody knife

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Shall play the empire, arbitrating that

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Which the commission of thy years and art

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Could to no issue of true honour bring.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Be not so long to speak. I long to die,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: If what thou speak’st speak not of remedy.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hold, daughter. I do spy a kind of hope,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Which craves as desperate an execution

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: As that is desperate which we would prevent.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: If, rather than to marry County Paris

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou hast the strength of will to slay thyself,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Then is it likely thou wilt undertake

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: A thing like death to chide away this shame,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: That cop’st with death himself to scape from it.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And if thou dar’st, I’ll give thee remedy.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O, bid me leap, rather than marry Paris,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: From off the battlements of yonder tower,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or walk in thievish ways, or bid me lurk

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Where serpents are. Chain me with roaring bears;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or hide me nightly in a charnel-house,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O’er-cover’d quite with dead men’s rattling bones,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: With reeky shanks and yellow chapless skulls.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or bid me go into a new-made grave,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And hide me with a dead man in his shroud;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Things that, to hear them told, have made me tremble,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And I will do it without fear or doubt,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To live an unstain’d wife to my sweet love.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hold then. Go home, be merry, give consent

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To marry Paris. Wednesday is tomorrow;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Tomorrow night look that thou lie alone,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Let not thy Nurse lie with thee in thy chamber.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Take thou this vial, being then in bed,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And this distilled liquor drink thou off,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: When presently through all thy veins shall run

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: A cold and drowsy humour; for no pulse

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Shall keep his native progress, but surcease.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: No warmth, no breath shall testify thou livest,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: The roses in thy lips and cheeks shall fade

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To paly ashes; thy eyes’ windows fall,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Like death when he shuts up the day of life.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Each part depriv’d of supple government,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Shall stiff and stark and cold appear like death.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And in this borrow’d likeness of shrunk death

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou shalt continue two and forty hours,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And then awake as from a pleasant sleep.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Now when the bridegroom in the morning comes

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To rouse thee from thy bed, there art thou dead.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Then as the manner of our country is,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: In thy best robes, uncover’d, on the bier,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Thou shalt be borne to that same ancient vault

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Where all the kindred of the Capulets lie.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: In the meantime, against thou shalt awake,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Shall Romeo by my letters know our drift,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And hither shall he come, and he and I

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Will watch thy waking, and that very night

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Shall Romeo bear thee hence to Mantua.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And this shall free thee from this present shame,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: If no inconstant toy nor womanish fear

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Abate thy valour in the acting it.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Give me, give me! O tell not me of fear!

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hold; get you gone, be strong and prosperous

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: In this resolve. I’ll send a friar with speed

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To Mantua, with my letters to thy lord.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Love give me strength, and strength shall help afford.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Farewell, dear father.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Capulet, Lady Capulet, Nurse and Servants.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: So many guests invite as here are writ.
[_Exit first Servant._]

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Sirrah, go hire me twenty cunning cooks.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: You shall have none ill, sir; for I’ll try if they can lick their

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: fingers.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: How canst thou try them so?

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: Marry, sir, ’tis an ill cook that cannot lick his own fingers;

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: therefore he that cannot lick his fingers goes not with me.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Go, begone.
[_Exit second Servant._]

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: We shall be much unfurnish’d for this time.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: What, is my daughter gone to Friar Lawrence?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Ay, forsooth.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Well, he may chance to do some good on her.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: A peevish self-will’d harlotry it is.
Enter Juliet.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: See where she comes from shrift with merry look.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: How now, my headstrong. Where have you been gadding?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Where I have learnt me to repent the sin

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Of disobedient opposition

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To you and your behests; and am enjoin’d

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: By holy Lawrence to fall prostrate here,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To beg your pardon. Pardon, I beseech you.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Henceforward I am ever rul’d by you.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Send for the County, go tell him of this.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I’ll have this knot knit up tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I met the youthful lord at Lawrence’ cell,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And gave him what becomed love I might,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Not stepping o’er the bounds of modesty.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Why, I am glad on’t. This is well. Stand up.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: This is as’t should be. Let me see the County.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Ay, marry. Go, I say, and fetch him hither.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Now afore God, this reverend holy Friar,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: All our whole city is much bound to him.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Nurse, will you go with me into my closet,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To help me sort such needful ornaments

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: As you think fit to furnish me tomorrow?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: No, not till Thursday. There is time enough.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Go, Nurse, go with her. We’ll to church tomorrow.
[_Exeunt Juliet and Nurse._]

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: We shall be short in our provision,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: ’Tis now near night.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Tush, I will stir about,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And all things shall be well, I warrant thee, wife.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Go thou to Juliet, help to deck up her.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I’ll not to bed tonight, let me alone.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I’ll play the housewife for this once.—What, ho!—

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: They are all forth: well, I will walk myself

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: To County Paris, to prepare him up

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Against tomorrow. My heart is wondrous light

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Since this same wayward girl is so reclaim’d.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Juliet and Nurse.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Ay, those attires are best. But, gentle Nurse,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I pray thee leave me to myself tonight;

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: For I have need of many orisons

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To move the heavens to smile upon my state,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Which, well thou know’st, is cross and full of sin.
Enter Lady Capulet.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: What, are you busy, ho? Need you my help?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: No, madam; we have cull’d such necessaries

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: As are behoveful for our state tomorrow.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: So please you, let me now be left alone,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And let the nurse this night sit up with you,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: For I am sure you have your hands full all

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: In this so sudden business.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Good night.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Get thee to bed and rest, for thou hast need.
[_Exeunt Lady Capulet and Nurse._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Farewell. God knows when we shall meet again.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I have a faint cold fear thrills through my veins

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That almost freezes up the heat of life.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I’ll call them back again to comfort me.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Nurse!—What should she do here?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: My dismal scene I needs must act alone.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Come, vial.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What if this mixture do not work at all?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Shall I be married then tomorrow morning?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: No, No! This shall forbid it. Lie thou there.
[_Laying down her dagger._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: What if it be a poison, which the Friar

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Subtly hath minister’d to have me dead,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Lest in this marriage he should be dishonour’d,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Because he married me before to Romeo?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I fear it is. And yet methinks it should not,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: For he hath still been tried a holy man.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: How if, when I am laid into the tomb,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I wake before the time that Romeo

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Come to redeem me? There’s a fearful point!

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Shall I not then be stifled in the vault,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: To whose foul mouth no healthsome air breathes in,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And there die strangled ere my Romeo comes?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Or, if I live, is it not very like,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: The horrible conceit of death and night,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Together with the terror of the place,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: As in a vault, an ancient receptacle,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Where for this many hundred years the bones

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Of all my buried ancestors are pack’d,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Where bloody Tybalt, yet but green in earth,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Lies festering in his shroud; where, as they say,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: At some hours in the night spirits resort—

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Alack, alack, is it not like that I,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: So early waking, what with loathsome smells,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And shrieks like mandrakes torn out of the earth,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That living mortals, hearing them, run mad.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O, if I wake, shall I not be distraught,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Environed with all these hideous fears,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And madly play with my forefathers’ joints?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And pluck the mangled Tybalt from his shroud?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And, in this rage, with some great kinsman’s bone,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: As with a club, dash out my desperate brains?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: O look, methinks I see my cousin’s ghost

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Seeking out Romeo that did spit his body

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Upon a rapier’s point. Stay, Tybalt, stay!

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Romeo, Romeo, Romeo, here’s drink! I drink to thee.
[_Throws herself on the bed._]
Enter Lady Capulet and Nurse.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Hold, take these keys and fetch more spices, Nurse.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: They call for dates and quinces in the pastry.
Enter Capulet.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Come, stir, stir, stir! The second cock hath crow’d,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: The curfew bell hath rung, ’tis three o’clock.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Look to the bak’d meats, good Angelica;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Spare not for cost.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Go, you cot-quean, go,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Get you to bed; faith, you’ll be sick tomorrow

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: For this night’s watching.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: No, not a whit. What! I have watch’d ere now

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: All night for lesser cause, and ne’er been sick.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Ay, you have been a mouse-hunt in your time;

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: But I will watch you from such watching now.
[_Exeunt Lady Capulet and Nurse._]

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: A jealous-hood, a jealous-hood!
Enter Servants, with spits, logs and baskets.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Now, fellow, what’s there?

lines.speaker: FIRST SERVANT
lines.text: Things for the cook, sir; but I know not what.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Make haste, make haste.
[_Exit First Servant._]

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: —Sirrah, fetch drier logs.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Call Peter, he will show thee where they are.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: I have a head, sir, that will find out logs

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: And never trouble Peter for the matter.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Mass and well said; a merry whoreson, ha.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Thou shalt be loggerhead.—Good faith, ’tis day.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: The County will be here with music straight,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: For so he said he would. I hear him near.
[_Play music._]

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Nurse! Wife! What, ho! What, Nurse, I say!
Re-enter Nurse.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Go waken Juliet, go and trim her up.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: I’ll go and chat with Paris. Hie, make haste,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Make haste; the bridegroom he is come already.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Make haste I say.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Juliet’s Chamber; Juliet on the bed.

lines.text: Enter Nurse.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Mistress! What, mistress! Juliet! Fast, I warrant her, she.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Why, lamb, why, lady, fie, you slug-abed!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Why, love, I say! Madam! Sweetheart! Why, bride!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: What, not a word? You take your pennyworths now.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Sleep for a week; for the next night, I warrant,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: The County Paris hath set up his rest

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: That you shall rest but little. God forgive me!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Marry and amen. How sound is she asleep!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I needs must wake her. Madam, madam, madam!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Ay, let the County take you in your bed,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: He’ll fright you up, i’faith. Will it not be?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: What, dress’d, and in your clothes, and down again?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: I must needs wake you. Lady! Lady! Lady!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Alas, alas! Help, help! My lady’s dead!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O, well-a-day that ever I was born.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Some aqua vitae, ho! My lord! My lady!
Enter Lady Capulet.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: What noise is here?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O lamentable day!

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: What is the matter?

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Look, look! O heavy day!

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: O me, O me! My child, my only life.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Revive, look up, or I will die with thee.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Help, help! Call help.
Enter Capulet.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: For shame, bring Juliet forth, her lord is come.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: She’s dead, deceas’d, she’s dead; alack the day!

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Alack the day, she’s dead, she’s dead, she’s dead!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Ha! Let me see her. Out alas! She’s cold,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Her blood is settled and her joints are stiff.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Life and these lips have long been separated.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Death lies on her like an untimely frost

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Upon the sweetest flower of all the field.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O lamentable day!

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: O woful time!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Death, that hath ta’en her hence to make me wail,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Ties up my tongue and will not let me speak.
Enter Friar Lawrence and Paris with Musicians.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Come, is the bride ready to go to church?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Ready to go, but never to return.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: O son, the night before thy wedding day

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Hath death lain with thy bride. There she lies,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Flower as she was, deflowered by him.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Death is my son-in-law, death is my heir;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: My daughter he hath wedded. I will die

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And leave him all; life, living, all is death’s.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Have I thought long to see this morning’s face,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: And doth it give me such a sight as this?

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Accurs’d, unhappy, wretched, hateful day.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: Most miserable hour that e’er time saw

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: In lasting labour of his pilgrimage.

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: But one, poor one, one poor and loving child,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: But one thing to rejoice and solace in,

lines.speaker: LADY CAPULET
lines.text: And cruel death hath catch’d it from my sight.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O woe! O woeful, woeful, woeful day.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Most lamentable day, most woeful day

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: That ever, ever, I did yet behold!

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O day, O day, O day, O hateful day.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Never was seen so black a day as this.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: O woeful day, O woeful day.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Beguil’d, divorced, wronged, spited, slain.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Most detestable death, by thee beguil’d,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: By cruel, cruel thee quite overthrown.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: O love! O life! Not life, but love in death!

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Despis’d, distressed, hated, martyr’d, kill’d.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Uncomfortable time, why cam’st thou now

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: To murder, murder our solemnity?

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: O child! O child! My soul, and not my child,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Dead art thou. Alack, my child is dead,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And with my child my joys are buried.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Peace, ho, for shame. Confusion’s cure lives not

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: In these confusions. Heaven and yourself

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Had part in this fair maid, now heaven hath all,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And all the better is it for the maid.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Your part in her you could not keep from death,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: But heaven keeps his part in eternal life.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: The most you sought was her promotion,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: For ’twas your heaven she should be advanc’d,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And weep ye now, seeing she is advanc’d

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Above the clouds, as high as heaven itself?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: O, in this love, you love your child so ill

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: That you run mad, seeing that she is well.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: She’s not well married that lives married long,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: But she’s best married that dies married young.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Dry up your tears, and stick your rosemary

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: On this fair corse, and, as the custom is,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And in her best array bear her to church;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: For though fond nature bids us all lament,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Yet nature’s tears are reason’s merriment.

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: All things that we ordained festival

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Turn from their office to black funeral:

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Our instruments to melancholy bells,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Our wedding cheer to a sad burial feast;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Our solemn hymns to sullen dirges change;

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: Our bridal flowers serve for a buried corse,

lines.speaker: CAPULET
lines.text: And all things change them to the contrary.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Sir, go you in, and, madam, go with him,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And go, Sir Paris, everyone prepare

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: To follow this fair corse unto her grave.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: The heavens do lower upon you for some ill;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Move them no more by crossing their high will.
[_Exeunt Capulet, Lady Capulet, Paris and Friar._]

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Faith, we may put up our pipes and be gone.

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: Honest good fellows, ah, put up, put up,

lines.speaker: NURSE
lines.text: For well you know this is a pitiful case.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Ay, by my troth, the case may be amended.
[_Exit Nurse._]
Enter Peter.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Musicians, O, musicians, ‘Heart’s ease,’ ‘Heart’s ease’, O, and you

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: will have me live, play ‘Heart’s ease.’

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Why ‘Heart’s ease’?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: O musicians, because my heart itself plays ‘My heart is full’. O play

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: me some merry dump to comfort me.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Not a dump we, ’tis no time to play now.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: You will not then?

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: I will then give it you soundly.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: What will you give us?

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: No money, on my faith, but the gleek! I will give you the minstrel.

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Then will I give you the serving-creature.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Then will I lay the serving-creature’s dagger on your pate. I will

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: carry no crotchets. I’ll re you, I’ll fa you. Do you note me?

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: And you re us and fa us, you note us.

lines.speaker: SECOND MUSICIAN
lines.text: Pray you put up your dagger, and put out your wit.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Then have at you with my wit. I will dry-beat you with an iron wit, and

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: put up my iron dagger. Answer me like men.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: ‘When griping griefs the heart doth wound,

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: And doleful dumps the mind oppress,

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Then music with her silver sound’—

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Why ‘silver sound’? Why ‘music with her silver sound’? What say you,

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Simon Catling?

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: Marry, sir, because silver hath a sweet sound.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Prates. What say you, Hugh Rebeck?

lines.speaker: SECOND MUSICIAN
lines.text: I say ‘silver sound’ because musicians sound for silver.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: Prates too! What say you, James Soundpost?

lines.speaker: THIRD MUSICIAN
lines.text: Faith, I know not what to say.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: O, I cry you mercy, you are the singer. I will say for you. It is

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: ‘music with her silver sound’ because musicians have no gold for

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: sounding.

lines.speaker: PETER
lines.text: ‘Then music with her silver sound

lines.speaker: PETER

[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST MUSICIAN
lines.text: What a pestilent knave is this same!

lines.speaker: SECOND MUSICIAN
lines.text: Hang him, Jack. Come, we’ll in here, tarry for the mourners, and stay

lines.text: dinner.

Enter Romeo.

lines.text: If I may trust the flattering eye of sleep,

lines.text: My bosom’s lord sits lightly in his throne;

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And all this day an unaccustom’d spirit

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Lifts me above the ground with cheerful thoughts.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I dreamt my lady came and found me dead,—

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Strange dream, that gives a dead man leave to think!—

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And breath’d such life with kisses in my lips,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: That I reviv’d, and was an emperor.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Ah me, how sweet is love itself possess’d,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: When but love’s shadows are so rich in joy.
Enter Balthasar.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: News from Verona! How now, Balthasar?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Dost thou not bring me letters from the Friar?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: How doth my lady? Is my father well?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: How fares my Juliet? That I ask again;

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: For nothing can be ill if she be well.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Then she is well, and nothing can be ill.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Her body sleeps in Capel’s monument,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And her immortal part with angels lives.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: I saw her laid low in her kindred’s vault,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And presently took post to tell it you.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: O pardon me for bringing these ill news,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Since you did leave it for my office, sir.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Is it even so? Then I defy you, stars!

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Thou know’st my lodging. Get me ink and paper,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And hire post-horses. I will hence tonight.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: I do beseech you sir, have patience.

lines.text: Your looks are pale and wild, and do import

lines.text: Some misadventure.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Tush, thou art deceiv’d.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Leave me, and do the thing I bid thee do.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Hast thou no letters to me from the Friar?

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: No, my good lord.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: No matter. Get thee gone,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And hire those horses. I’ll be with thee straight.
[_Exit Balthasar._]

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Well, Juliet, I will lie with thee tonight.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Let’s see for means. O mischief thou art swift

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: To enter in the thoughts of desperate men.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I do remember an apothecary,—

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And hereabouts he dwells,—which late I noted

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: In tatter’d weeds, with overwhelming brows,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Culling of simples, meagre were his looks,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Sharp misery had worn him to the bones;

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And in his needy shop a tortoise hung,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: An alligator stuff’d, and other skins

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Of ill-shaped fishes; and about his shelves

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: A beggarly account of empty boxes,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Green earthen pots, bladders, and musty seeds,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Remnants of packthread, and old cakes of roses

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Were thinly scatter’d, to make up a show.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Noting this penury, to myself I said,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And if a man did need a poison now,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Whose sale is present death in Mantua,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Here lives a caitiff wretch would sell it him.

lines.text: O, this same thought did but forerun my need,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And this same needy man must sell it me.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: As I remember, this should be the house.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Being holiday, the beggar’s shop is shut.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: What, ho! Apothecary!
Enter Apothecary.

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: Who calls so loud?

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Come hither, man. I see that thou art poor.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Hold, there is forty ducats. Let me have

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: A dram of poison, such soon-speeding gear

lines.text: As will disperse itself through all the veins,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: That the life-weary taker may fall dead,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And that the trunk may be discharg’d of breath

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: As violently as hasty powder fir’d

lines.text: Doth hurry from the fatal cannon’s womb.

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: Such mortal drugs I have, but Mantua’s law

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: Is death to any he that utters them.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Art thou so bare and full of wretchedness,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: And fear’st to die? Famine is in thy cheeks,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Need and oppression starveth in thine eyes,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Contempt and beggary hangs upon thy back.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: The world is not thy friend, nor the world’s law;

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: The world affords no law to make thee rich;

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Then be not poor, but break it and take this.

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: My poverty, but not my will consents.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I pay thy poverty, and not thy will.

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: Put this in any liquid thing you will

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: And drink it off; and, if you had the strength

lines.speaker: APOTHECARY
lines.text: Of twenty men, it would despatch you straight.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: There is thy gold, worse poison to men’s souls,

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Doing more murder in this loathsome world

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Than these poor compounds that thou mayst not sell.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: I sell thee poison, thou hast sold me none.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Farewell, buy food, and get thyself in flesh.

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: Come, cordial and not poison, go with me

lines.speaker: ROMEO
lines.text: To Juliet’s grave, for there must I use thee.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Friar John.

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Holy Franciscan Friar! Brother, ho!
Enter Friar Lawrence.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: This same should be the voice of Friar John.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Welcome from Mantua. What says Romeo?

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Or, if his mind be writ, give me his letter.

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Going to find a barefoot brother out,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: One of our order, to associate me,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Here in this city visiting the sick,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: And finding him, the searchers of the town,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Suspecting that we both were in a house

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Where the infectious pestilence did reign,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Seal’d up the doors, and would not let us forth,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: So that my speed to Mantua there was stay’d.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Who bare my letter then to Romeo?

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: I could not send it,—here it is again,—

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Nor get a messenger to bring it thee,

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: So fearful were they of infection.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Unhappy fortune! By my brotherhood,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: The letter was not nice, but full of charge,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Of dear import, and the neglecting it

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: May do much danger. Friar John, go hence,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Get me an iron crow and bring it straight

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Unto my cell.

lines.speaker: FRIAR JOHN
lines.text: Brother, I’ll go and bring it thee.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Now must I to the monument alone.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Within this three hours will fair Juliet wake.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: She will beshrew me much that Romeo

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Hath had no notice of these accidents;

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: But I will write again to Mantua,

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: And keep her at my cell till Romeo come.

lines.speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
lines.text: Poor living corse, clos’d in a dead man’s tomb.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: A churchyard; in it a Monument belonging to the Capulets.

lines.text: Enter Paris, and his Page bearing flowers and a torch.

lines.text: Give me thy torch, boy. Hence and stand aloof.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Yet put it out, for I would not be seen.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Under yond yew tree lay thee all along,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Holding thy ear close to the hollow ground;

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: So shall no foot upon the churchyard tread,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Being loose, unfirm, with digging up of graves,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: But thou shalt hear it. Whistle then to me,

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: As signal that thou hear’st something approach.

lines.speaker: PARIS
lines.text: Give me those flowers. Do as I bid thee, go.
